The wandering of crack smokers in the Paris metro poses such problems that some trains sometimes stop at stations. A worrying phenomenon.

Station Jules-Joffrin (XVIII), on line 12, direction Aubervilliers. In the late afternoon of January, the man with the hollowed-out face, with his eyes encircled, floating in his worn-out trousers, enters, haggardly, the uncertain gait, into the subway train marking the stop. He pulls a jump seat and sits down, a lit rolled cigarette in his left hand, a crack pipe in the right. He scarcely draws a few glances from a handful of travelers, despite the smell of tobacco spreading on the train.

Especially lines 4 and 12

A few minutes later, he went down to the next station, Marcadet-Poissonniers, to join a group of six men, sitting along the wall.

All are crackers, crack consumers. Sometimes with their companions of misfortune, they haunt since years the metro stations of north-east Paris. Lines 4 and 12, especially. Wandering tirelessly between Jules-Joffrin, Marcadet-Poissoniers, Marx-Dormoy, Simplon, Porte-de-la-Chapelle. Chased from their former territories of the Stalingrad place (19th) or from the North station (Xe) by the successive eviction operations, they entrenched themselves in the basement, paved with sidewalks during the installation, in 2012 , of the first priority security zone (ZSP) Barbès-Château-Rouge, by Manuel Valls, then Minister of the Interior.

Where are they?

Drivers no longer stop at certain stations

For more than three years, all the initiatives taken in partnership with the police headquarters and the RATP to get these metro addicts out and ensure their health care have partially failed in the long term. Despite the involvement of drug addiction associations. Each time, the crackers are down on the docks. And the situation has become explosive, to the point, that at the call of the Unsa-RATP, some train drivers of the line 12 have recently decided not to mark the stop at some stations, when the platforms are invaded addicts. A question of security. Theirs and that of users.

"I find the situation worrying"

"When I see them, I see death. Aïssa, daily user of the station Marx-Dormoy (XVIII) can not find her words when she evokes "those people who turned into zombies, pulling on their pipe". "Am I scared? she wonders, no, I do not think so. In any case, not an aggression because they are stone most of the time. But I find the situation anxiety: they are there from morning to night, sitting or lying in the station, smoking or preparing their products. Sometimes they start screaming without knowing why. Or fight each other. Clearly, the passengers all gather on the opposite side of the wharf ... "
